clue.text: Delay is what upset art gallery

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means overturned, so the two short words before it are read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
eh? is what you say when you want something repeated, just like what?
the Tate is a family of British art galleries, the best known in London

explanation.surface: A hold-up is the thing that annoyed the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IS EH, read as one run, into HESI. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: both mean to pause or hold back before acting.

clue.text: Author risks getting involved with 22

indicators.note: getting involved suggests the two sets of letters become tangled up with each other

parts.note: taken as written
22 points to the answer at 22 across, BONAPARTE, whose nine letters are used

explanation.surface: A writer's gambles get tangled up with whatever is at number 22.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' is a cross-reference: the answer at 22 across, BONAPARTE, joins RISKS as the letters that 'getting involved with' mixes together.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: he was the Russian poet and novelist who wrote Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: To stand up used to be hard

parts.note: what used to be is what was
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Getting to one's feet was once a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is idiomatic: an excuse that does not stand up is one that fails to convince.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an alibi or excuse that survives scrutiny and convinces people is said to do either.

clue.text: Blushing after maiden tucks into flaky pies made with mince

indicators.note: after says the word for blushing comes behind the rest
tucks into says the letter for maiden is slipped inside the reworked pies
flaky means crumbling or unreliable, so the letters of pies fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, one with no runs scored
someone blushing is red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone goes red after a young woman starts on crumbly pastries filled with ground meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaky' makes SIPE from the pastries, 'tucks into' opens it for the maiden, and blushing comes 'after'. The definition is whimsical: mincing is affected daintiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: to mince is to behave with affected daintiness, and a coy, affected smile is one produced that way.

clue.text: Old stick, when it's caught fire

parts.note: ex means former, as an old flame is an ex

indicators.note: caught says the word for stick has trapped the short word inside itself

parts.note: to cement things is to stick them together
it's is short for it is; only the letters of it are used

explanation.surface: An old piece of wood, once lit, went up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is a container signal, nothing to do with catching fire. 'stick' is the verb, to glue, and 'fire' is the figurative kind, ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the figurative sense: fire is passion or ardour, the thrill that stirs people up.

clue.text: Result of a bit of mischief

definitions.meaning: the effect or consequence that something has
whimsically, one deed done by a little devil: a three-letter sprite followed by a three-letter deed

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a straight synonym for an effect or consequence; the other whimsically splits the word into a mischievous sprite and its deed.

clue.text: Actor recalled keeping Arab as number one fan

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the turned surname has the Arab inside it
recalled means brought back, so the actor's surname is written backwards

parts.note: Nicolas Cage is an American film actor
an Omani is a person from Oman, an Arab country

explanation.surface: A performer is remembered for retaining an Arab as his most devoted admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives EGAC, which is 'keeping' the Arab. Number one is slang for oneself, so this fan adores himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone obsessed with themselves is a devoted admirer of number one, slang for oneself.

clue.text: Tea cups in this?

indicators.note: cups as a verb means holds in cupped hands, so the tea word goes round the next piece

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of crockery tea cups come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' is a verb here, not crockery: CHA holds IN. The whole clue then describes the answer, with 'this' standing for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain crockery: the whole clue describes it, since a tea service is typically made of the stuff.

clue.text: By yard, lemon drops on wood

parts.note: by is the multiplication sign in dimensions, as in two by four, written X

indicators.note: drops says the word lemon lets go of the two letters named next

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: the letters that lemon loses

explanation.surface: Sharp yellow sweets are scattered over the timber, a yard at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lemon drops on' is LEMON letting go of ON, not a bag of sweets, leaving LEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term: the woody tissue of a plant that carries water up from the roots.

clue.text: Holiday to take, and a temperature which drops?

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
to sit an exam is British usage for to take one
that can replace which as a relative pronoun, as in the book which or that I read

explanation.surface: A break to enjoy, along with a thermometer reading that falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like the temperature falling, but it is the definition: someone who drops a subject says no more about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who drops a matter says no more about it and lets it rest.

clue.text: One setter, wise one, recycled?

indicators.note: recycled says a letter is cycled round from one end of the sage's name to the other

parts.note: a rishi is a Hindu sage or holy seer

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler, a clever one, has been reused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' moves the last I of RISHI to the front. The setter is a gun dog, not a crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the red-coated gun dog from Ireland is one breed among several.

clue.text: Proper soldier hugging one's mum for the first time

indicators.note: hugging means the two words together wrap their arms round the next piece

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier in a parachute regiment
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is not used

explanation.surface: A well-behaved serviceman embraces his mother, something he has never done before.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term: a woman who is giving birth, or has given birth, to her earliest child.

clue.text: Meet in lift

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning fitting or suitable, as in meet and right
a slang verb meaning to steal or take for oneself

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means suitable, the old sense of meet; as a verb it means to take without permission, which is to lift.

clue.text: People mostly raved about getting partly covered

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of people is used

parts.note: taken as written, less its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of the crowd enthused over being half hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PEOPLE to PEOPL, and 'about' rearranges PEOPL with RAVED. 'getting' simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: things that lay with one edge on top of the next each hid a portion of it.

clue.text: Have 23d each time

parts.note: ea is the abbreviation for each, as on price lists

explanation.surface: Take whatever is at 23 down on every occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: '23d' refers to the answer at 23 down, MEAL: to have a meal is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer at 23 down is a serving of food, and to have one is to consume it.

clue.text: Mostly gentle incline in area of London

indicators.note: mostly means the word for gentle loses its last letter

parts.note: easy means gentle, as in an easy slope or go easy on him
to incline to something is to tend towards it

explanation.surface: A largely mild slope in one district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims EASY to EAS. 'incline' is the verb, to lean towards, not a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A place name: the traditionally working-class district of the capital, home of the Cockneys.

clue.text: After visit, family's good

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them, as in go and see your aunt
kin are your family and relations

explanation.surface: Once the trip is over, the relatives are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word placing the pieces, but it is the definition: to be after something is to be hunting for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to be after something is to be looking for or pursuing it.

clue.text: They provide light and roll joints for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade first letters

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll
seams are the joints where pieces of fabric or metal meet

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a lighter and rolls cannabis cigarettes for the Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal description: they are rays or shafts of sunshine.

clue.text: How is one "high" integer over 1000?

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the rearranged word sits above the last letter
high can mean intoxicated and out of control, so the letters of the next word are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
G is short for a grand, slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a whole number above a thousand can be called high.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is sneaky: 'How' is one example of the answer. 'high' rearranges INTEGER to GREETIN, which stands 'over' G.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: 'How' is the stock salutation of Native Americans in old westerns, so it is one way of saying hello.

clue.text: With and without name, one's suffering

indicators.note: without says the letter for name is missing from the word after it

parts.note: one taken as written; the 's is not used

explanation.surface: Whether identified or anonymous, a person is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With and without' reads as one phrase but does two jobs in turn: an abbreviation, then 'without' removing a letter to leave OE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean grief, misery or distress.

clue.text: PC device with extra battery, cable, adapter, mains leads?

indicators.note: leads are the letters in front, so each of the six words before it gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A computer gadget that comes with a spare battery and assorted power cords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' looks like more electrical cables, but it asks for the first letters of the six words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small video camera attached to or built into a computer for video calls.

clue.text: Criminal finally treated in a criminal compound

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it
criminal as an adjective means wrong or lawless, so the three words before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook is at last given medical care inside a lawless enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Criminal' only gives its last letter L; the second is the anagram signal, rearranging TREATED IN A. 'compound' is chemical, not a prison yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemistry example: a poisonous salt made from a heavy metal and nitric acid.

clue.text: Goldfinger demands respect, Richard said

indicators.note: said tells you the two words before it are spoken, and the answer is what you hear

parts.note: awe is deep respect mixed with wonder; Rick is a short form of Richard

explanation.surface: The Bond villain insists on deference, according to Richard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes 'awe, Rick' a soundalike. Goldfinger is the Bond villain, whose first name is the answer; 'demands' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the Bond villain Goldfinger, chosen by Ian Fleming because the word means relating to gold.

clue.text: Live outside next to isolated emperor

indicators.note: outside says the word for live goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
on can mean next to, as in a town on the river
apart means separated or isolated from others

explanation.surface: Dwell outdoors beside a lonely ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal, not the open air. The isolated emperor nods to Napoleon's exile on St Helena.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Napoleon, who crowned himself ruler of the French empire in 1804.

clue.text: Piece from opera company including biblical stories

indicators.note: including says the opera company has the next piece inside it

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Opera in New York
OT is the Old Testament, the first part of the Bible

explanation.surface: An excerpt from an opera troupe's show that takes in tales from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a short sacred choral composition, so a work of music.

clue.text: A little time allowed for food

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short period is set aside to have something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'food' alone: the answer is a noun, and 'for' only joins the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an occasion of eating, or the dishes served at one.

clue.text: Empty notebook found in beer joint

indicators.note: found in says the emptied word sits inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: empty means the notebook loses its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A blank jotter turns up in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves NK from NOTEBOOK, which is 'found in' ALE. A beer joint is a bar, but 'joint' alone is the definition, a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the hinge of the body connecting the foot to the leg.

clue.text: What 7 could be

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the other answer might be arranged differently to make this one

parts.note: 7 refers to the answer at 7 across, EGOMANIAC, whose nine letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the thing at number 7 might turn out to be.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is the answer at 7 across, EGOMANIAC, which 'could be' rearranged. 'What' alone is the definition, as in 'What?'
explanation.definitionFit: Both are things you say when you did not catch a remark and want it repeated.
